thread:
jia: Heads-up — seeing weird KV behavior on canary. overall KV hit rate dropped ~20% and resident mem keeps climbing over long contexts. dumped a few sample keys, looks like session-prefixing sometimes collapses to a common namespace and we end up reusing/overwriting entries across sessions.

michael: Can you paste the sample keys? curious how the namespace is constructed.

jia: sure. examples from the dump:
```
kv:key:prefix:sess:session-abc123:model:gpt-3.2:pos:0
kv:key:prefix:sess::model:gpt-3.2:pos:0   <-- missing session id
kv:key:prefix:user:user-99:model:gpt-3.2:pos:0
kv:key:prefix:sess:session-xyz789:model:gpt-3.2:pos:0
```
note the second one — empty session field. our sticky-routing rewrite seems to write 'sess' but not guard empty ids, so they collapse to the same key.

alexa: ah yep that's from the sticky-routing PR (ref PR: https://git.redwood/dev/r/1234). we added a path rewrite to keep 'sess' in the key for routing visibility. oops if session id is absent we still left the token.

sam: that explains the high fragmentation + eviction noise. which metrics moved?

jia: evictions_per_min spiked from ~12 -> ~180 on canary, kv_hit_rate fell 88% -> 68%, p95 latency increased 30ms. memory footprint for kv store up ~22% for same workload. stack trace points to frequent prefix churn rather than retained large entries.

dina: mitigation ideas:
- qualify keys with tenant id + model version + key schema version
- sanitize empty session -> use 'sessless' sentinel
- short hash suffix instead of full prefix for long requests

michael: agree. propose new key spec v2:
```
kv:v2:{tenant}:{model}:{schema_v}:{session_or_sessless}:{prefix_hash}
# example: kv:v2:acme:gpt-3.2:1:sess-abc123:4f2b
```
write path will emit v2 alongside v1 for N days (write-through) and we expose a metric kv_key_version{v2=1} to track adoption.

jia: ran a local canary with v2 keys + session sanitization. results: kv_hit_rate back to 92%, evictions drop to 15/min, p50 token latency -8%. memory growth stabilized for longctx scenarios.

alexa: rollout plan?

michael: canary -> 10% -> 50% -> full. migration window 7 days. also need backfill/warm-up for hot prefixes: we should pre-warm v2 keys for active sessions during rollout.

sam: i'll run a k6 load script to simulate many small sessions and long-context sessions to ensure fragmentation doesn't regress. also recommend a TTL policy variant: longctx TTLs should be longer but pinned to session activity, not absolute lifetime.

jia: opening PR with changes + feature flag (runtime.kv.key_version = 'v2' & runtime.kv.sanitize_empty_session = true). adding dashboard panels for key_version usage, prefix_coalescence_rate, and sentinel_count. will post link when ready.

michael: thanks. @infra-bot can we schedule a canary deploy for next sprint and add an alert if evictions/min > 50?

infra-bot: noted — created ticket INF-872, canary window scheduled, alert rule added (evictions_per_min > 50). :white_check_mark:

alexa: nice catch, jia. big win if v2 holds. :thumbsup:
